Tags: photography, photo_editing, lightroom, photography_ai, lens

> Most editing machines ask you to choose: power or portability. The GMKtec EVO-X1 Pro is interesting because it barely asks at all. This is a full desktop editing computer that measures 107 x 111 x 63mm and weighs 590g — lighter than a 70-200mm lens, and small enough to genuinely live in a corner of a camera bag. For anyone who has wanted a proper editing machine on location without hauling a laptop that throttles or a tower that doesn’t travel, that’s a proposition worth a look. You can find it on the GMKtec store. What it actually does for photo work Inside is AMD’s Ryzen AI 9 HX 470: 12 cores, 24 threads, boosting to 5.2GHz, with Radeon 890M integrated graphics and a 55 TOPS neural processor (86 TOPS across the platform). ## [Framework Desktop: the repairable, Linux-friendly AI mini PC for open-source creatives](https://camerajabber.com/photography-news/framework-desktop-the-repairable-linux-friendly-ai-mini-pc-for-open-source-creatives/)
*Camera Jabber* | 31/07/2026 | Score: 1.00
Tags: photography, photo_editing

> The Framework Desktop takes the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 in a very different direction from the sealed boxes elsewhere in this roundup. Built around a 4.5-litre Mini-ITX chassis with a standard FlexATX power supply and support for standard 120mm CPU fans, it’s the machine for creatives who want to open it up, upgrade it, and — crucially — run it on Linux. For open-source and repair-minded photographers and editors, it’s the obvious pick. See it at Framework. That standard-parts, Linux-friendly design shapes which software suits it best, and it happens to be a superb home for the open-source creative stack. darktable, the open-source RAW developer that leans on OpenCL GPU acceleration, runs beautifully on the Radeon 8060S; RawTherapee offers another powerful, free RAW path; GIMP covers pixel editing; and Krita gives digital painters a GPU-accelerated canvas. None of these ties you to a subscription, and all run natively on Linux...
